content.text:
I found 10 households where an owner's 2025 required minimum distribution (RMD) was not met, as of the 15 April 2026 records. They fall into two groups.

**1. The 401(k) share was paid out of an IRA instead (5 owners, all turning 73 in 2025).** Each signed a form (recorded in the CRM) to take the RMDs for two IRAs and a former employer's 401(k) "added together" as one payment from an IRA. Each payment exactly equals the combined figure, but IRAs can't be combined with a 401(k): the 401(k)'s RMD has to come out of the 401(k) itself. None of these 401(k)s paid anything out by the 1 April 2026 deadline for a first RMD year. The IRA share itself was fully covered.

| Household | Owner | 401(k) | 401(k) balance at 31 Dec 2024 | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0120 | Laila Udeh | SYN-01200004 | 333,434.59 | 12,582.44 |
| HH-0236 | Xavier Santangelo | SYN-02360004 | 290,330.91 | 10,955.88 |
| HH-0664 | Freya Chaudhry | SYN-06640004 | 292,023.18 | 11,019.74 |
| HH-0371 | Rosa Tamura | SYN-03710004 | 401,852.77 | 15,164.26 |
| HH-5271 | Teodoro Villanueva | SYN-52710004 | 337,343.96 | 12,729.96 |

**2. Inherited IRAs with nothing taken in 2025 (5 owners).** In each case the original owner had already started RMDs before dying, according to the prior custodian's confirmation in the CRM. The heir is a child more than 10 years younger, so they must take yearly RMDs during the 10-year payout window. The IRS waived these for 2021–2024 but not for 2025. None of these accounts shows any 2025 distribution, and the deadline was 31 December 2025.

| Household | Heir | Inherited IRA | Divisor | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0607 | Noor Santangelo | SYN-06070002 | 31.3 | 11,760.82 |
| HH-0842 | Ines Trevelyan | SYN-08420002 | 45.7 | 7,090.19 |
| HH-0491 | Orla Jablonski | SYN-04910002 | 21.7 | 14,976.93 |
| HH-7126 | Samuel Adeyemi | SYN-71260002 | 35.2 | 10,757.24 |
| HH-0466 | Zainab Aldana | SYN-04660002 | 30.5 | 15,068.66 |

**What to check before acting:**
- **Divisors and the inherited group:** I computed every shortfall from the 31 Dec 2024 holdings plus cash. The divisors come from the IRS life-expectancy tables, not from these files: 26.5 at age 73, and each heir's own life expectancy reduced by one each year since the first year after the death. Group 2 also assumes "IRA owners" includes heirs who own inherited IRAs; if you meant only people's own IRAs, the answer is the five in group 1.
- **Recomputed totals:** For every other owner who had a 2025 RMD (HH-0168, 0190, 0222, 0410, 0414, 0445, 0555, 0637, 0782, 0885, 0989, 5814, 6047, 6590 and Una Lindgren in HH-0642), what was taken, including charitable gifts paid straight from the IRA, matched or exceeded the amount I recomputed.
- **Excluded:** Five other inherited IRAs had owners who died before starting RMDs, so no yearly amount was due. The spouses who died in 2025 had no IRA of their own.

I found 10 households where an owner's 2025 required minimum distribution (RMD) was not met, as of the 15 April 2026 records. They fall into two groups.

**1. The 401(k) share was paid out of an IRA instead (5 owners, all turning 73 in 2025).** Each signed a form (recorded in the CRM) to take the RMDs for two IRAs and a former employer's 401(k) "added together" as one payment from an IRA. Each payment exactly equals the combined figure, but IRAs can't be combined with a 401(k): the 401(k)'s RMD has to come out of the 401(k) itself. None of these 401(k)s paid anything out by the 1 April 2026 deadline for a first RMD year. The IRA share itself was fully covered.
